name: Calf stretch
pattern: Static hold: the shin moves forward over a flat foot, lengthening the calf and Achilles. Knee straight hits the gastrocnemius; knee bent hits the soleus.
setup: Face a wall, hands on it at chest height.
Step one foot back, heel flat, toes pointing straight at the wall.
Front knee bent, back knee straight.

steps.text: Lean the hips toward the wall until you feel the back calf pull.
Stay still 15-30 s, heel down. Then bend the back knee a little to move the stretch low, into the soleus.
Come out slowly, then switch sides.

cues.cue: Back heel stays flat on the floor.
cues.why: Once the heel lifts the ankle stops bending and the stretch is lost.

cues.cue: Straight knee for the upper calf, bend it about 20-30° for the lower calf.
cues.why: About 20° of knee bend fully takes the gastrocnemius out, leaving the soleus to stretch.
A turned-out foot lets the arch roll in and spreads the stretch away from the calf.

cues.cue: Ease in to a mild pull, never pain.
cues.why: Gentle stretches still gain range; stretching into pain did not help and can irritate the muscle.

cues.cue: Hold 15-30 s, 2-4 times, about 60 s in total per side.
cues.why: 30 s holds gave the same gains as 60 s; aim for at least 5 min per muscle each week, most days.

cues.cue: Best after training. Before, keep it under 60 s per muscle and finish with a dynamic warm-up.
cues.why: Short holds cost almost no strength or power; long holds (60 s or more) do. Stretching does not speed recovery.

breathing: Breathe slowly and normally. Ease a little deeper as you breathe out.

tempo.note: Ease in for about 3 s, hold 15-30 s, ease out. Repeat 2-4 times each side.

mistakes.name: Heel lifts
mistakes.looks: The back heel rises off the floor as you lean in.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the step until the heel stays down.
mistakes.why: No ankle bend means no calf stretch.

mistakes.name: Foot turned out
mistakes.looks: The back toes point out to the side.
mistakes.fix: Turn the toes to face the wall.
mistakes.why: The arch collapses and the calf is not lined up with the stretch.

mistakes.name: Bouncing
mistakes.looks: You bob in and out of the stretch instead of holding still.
mistakes.fix: Ease in slowly, then stay still and let it relax.
mistakes.why: Bouncing triggers the muscle to tighten back and can strain it.

safety: Achilles pain: keep it gentle, no heel drops off a step until it settles.
Hanging heel drops load the tendon: hold a rail and use both feet first.

variants.change: Back knee bent about 20-30°: stretch moves to the soleus and Achilles. Dorsiflexion rises by roughly 15°.
Seated, strap around the ball of the foot: pull the toes toward you, knee straight.
Contract-relax: push gently against the stretch for 3-6 s, relax, then ease deeper. Similar range gains to static holds; also best after training.
A partner moves the limb. Go slowly and say when you feel a mild pull; the partner holds there, never pushes into pain.
Moving version: controlled swings through the range, 8-12 reps. Better before training than long holds.

subtypes.name: Shin stretch
subtypes.change: Kneel on the tops of your feet and sit back, or point the foot behind you. Front of the shin stretches.

subtypes.name: Step heel drop
subtypes.change: Stand on the edge of a step, hold a rail; let one heel sink below the step, knee straight.

subtypes.name: Seated calf stretch
subtypes.change: Sit with the leg straight, strap or hands around the ball of the foot; pull the toes toward you.

subtypes.name: Bent-knee calf stretch
subtypes.match: achilles|crouch|squat|bent knee|knee to box|semi flexed|kneeling heel
subtypes.change: Same as the wall stretch but bend the back knee, heel down. Feel it low, near the heel.

metrics.label: Movement during hold
metrics.good: < 3° once you are in the stretch

motion.basis: Ankle dorsiflexion ranges from baumbach2014 (weight-bearing about 25° knee straight, 39° knee bent; 20° knee bend removes the gastrocnemius). Other angles estimated from the wall stance. Dose from garber2011, bandy1994, thomas2018.
